algorithm.Title: Mosquito Bite - Male (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Male
Definition: Qatar-localized UAT-only adult and pediatric pathway for mosquito bites, screening for anaphylaxis, infection and travel-related febrile disease; not approved for production.
FirstAid: Call Qatar 999 and do not drive. Use only the patient's own prescribed adrenaline auto-injector according to its plan and dispatcher instructions; keep the patient lying unless breathing is difficult. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Are throat or tongue swelling, breathing difficulty, faintness, confusion, or collapse the main concern?
questions.Information: Systemic allergic-reaction features require the Anaphylaxis pathway.

questions.Question: Are the lips, mouth, throat, or tongue suddenly swollen, is the person struggling to breathe, or has anyone lost consciousness or become floppy?
questions.Information: NHS.UK insect bites and stings guidance lists these as signs of a serious allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) requiring an immediate 999 call.

questions.Question: Is there fever, chills, or feeling generally unwell following recent travel to an area with mosquito-borne disease risk (e.g. malaria, dengue)?
questions.Information: Fever after travel-related mosquito exposure needs prompt evaluation to rule out mosquito-borne illness - a standard travel-medicine caution beyond the source page's own bite-specific criteria.

questions.Question: Is the skin around the bite hot, red, and painful, or leaking pus or fluid (signs of infection)?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance flags these infection signs as needing a pharmacist or primary-care review.

questions.Question: Are these typical itchy mosquito bites with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes minor bites without infection or allergy signs as manageable at home.

advice.Title: Emergency allergic reaction precautions
Content: Call Qatar 999 and do not drive. Use only the patient's own prescribed adrenaline auto-injector according to its plan and dispatcher instructions; keep the patient lying unless breathing is difficult. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: symptoms persist or recur; loss of consciousness.

advice.Title: Urgent travel-fever review
Content: Arrange prompt medical evaluation for fever following travel to a mosquito-borne disease risk area - mention the travel history clearly.
Call Back If: fever worsens; new symptoms develop.

advice.Title: Routine bite follow-up
Content: Keep the area clean and book a routine review for signs of infection.
Call Back If: increasing redness or pain.

advice.Title: Review for presumed mosquito bites
Content: Avoid scratching, clean the area gently and arrange clinician/pharmacist review before medication selection. Record travel precisely and escalate any fever or systemic symptom.
Call Back If: infection, bleeding or widespread rash; fever, confusion, vomiting or dehydration.

references: NHS.UK, "Insect bites and stings", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/insect-bites-and-stings/ (page last reviewed 01 June 2023)
